headline: High school social studies proposal would add a year-long personal finance and civics course, now headed to Policy Committee
summary: The course would combine one semester of personal finance with one semester of civics and government. Current policy requires three social studies courses covering global or world studies, early US history, and modern US and world history. The update said the work is ongoing, and a draft will go to the Policy Committee after review with Drummond Woodsum. A separate update set targets that 100% of seniors have a plan before graduating and 70% of eligible seniors complete the FAFSA.
discussion: Postsecondary planning follow-through: Members asked how to help students follow through on their plans after graduation. The presentation said counselors report that students who need the most support often struggle to follow through, and the team will discuss supports after graduation.
Deering data: A question was raised about 25% of seniors applying to a postsecondary option while 31% applied to college. The presentation said it would follow up with the team on the figures.

Students facing the biggest challenges: Members asked which groups face the most difficulty in planning. The presentation said multilingual students and students from low-income families face the most challenges, including language barriers and families unfamiliar with the steps.

Standardizing planning across schools: A member asked why the three high schools use different models. The presentation said the curriculum will be standardized, while delivery will fit each school's schedule and structure.

Earlier civics access: A question was raised about whether students can learn civics before the required course. The presentation said middle school design work and social studies design in the strategic plan could allow more vertical alignment.
